In a Fucked Up Situation (tm) - anything from being stuck as a civilian in a war zone to a post apocalyptic long term dystopia, the line between what constitutes 'currency' and barterable items is going to be somewhat blurry:

Barter is a relatively efficient way to deal with a fucked up situation; goods and services. Besides, you are going to prioritize immediately useful and more pedestrian stuff:

Toilet paper, soap, canned food (not too heavy by the way, and a can is a pretty neat unit of exchange - also unlike other kind of food, it is quite visible if it has been tampered with), any kind of fuel (wood, coal, gasoline, etc. can also be transported and neatly parceled for barter purposes); basic hand tools are also going to be objects intrinsically useful and usable for exchanges.

Ammunitions although useful might not be as critical as the previous items; in a fucked up situation your main priority is survival, not engaging in an all out shooting war with your neighbors; the odds are high you won't survive any shoot out - remember, in the absence of medical services, any kind of injury is going to be fatal - you should be in 'conflict avoidance mode'; you want some means of defending yourself, but just enough to get yourself out of a bad situation, that doesn't necessarily require a huge amount of ammunitions; besides it's heavy, not something you want to carry in large quantities at the expense of more useful stuff (like food) if you need to be on the move; and you might want to keep it low key too; do you really want to be too conspicuously armed if stuck as a civilian in a war zone? not sure it would be the first stuff I'd want to barter partly for that reason.

Medications go bad and can too easily be faked/tampered with, so I wouldn't trust it much as a unit of exchange/barter when dealing with people I don't trust.

I have spent way too much time thinking over stuff like this; may be from listening to old folks who actually went through this shit.

edit/ps: article of clothing, in particular shoes; everything else is relatively easy to mend, improvise and/or adapt; but shoes is more difficult to get right; I like the idea of tobacco; especially as a non smoker :-) it's light and wouldn't be too much of a burden to carry around.
